desc: Ideation: order preservation, gap non-increasing, prefix-sum operation view, reverse-operation view, counterexample showing max-distance matching insufficient ([1,5,6]→{5,5,6} needs 6 ops not 4).
Write brute-force investigation tool: enumerate achievable maps for small N,k; compare against candidate class; test (P,R) pairs for min-k mismatches.

Run the investigation program and analyze results: achievable maps are a strict subset of monotone 1-Lipschitz with |d|≤k; whole-domain sufficiency fails (k=1 cannot realize +1,+1,0,0,0); restriction to piece positions still insufficient ([1,5,6] witness); extra invariant is blocking/round-trip surcharge from nested displacements.

Derive and brute-force-validate the exact min-k formula via BFS ground truth: test crossing/round-trip surcharge hypotheses (interval-containment of other pieces' starts/dests; sweep-decomposition total-variation model) until zero mismatches on small random cases; must give 6 for [1,5,6]→{5,5,6}, 3 and 5 for samples 1 and 3.

Based on the validated formula, design O(N) or O(N log N) algorithm per test: greedy order-preserving assignment of pieces to B-squares (cover all, extras stack on nearest) minimizing the correct sweep cost, likely via two pointers plus a stack/DP over the direction sequence d_t = sign(R[t]−P[t]) with no "− before +" pattern.

Implement final Python solution with fast I/O (read all stdin, split), O(sum N) total; verify by reasoning against samples (3, -1, 5) and the [1,5,6] case (6); replace the current binary-search max-distance scaffold which is known to be wrong on blocking cases.
